## Verdict and scope

**Semantic verdict: equivalent to the frozen primary claim. Publication disposition: revise the supplement's mathematical typesetting before acceptance.** The review covers all 153 non-generated declarations in the exact inventory, their author-supplied statements and explanations, both assembled manuscripts, and the sole external citation. There are no configured generated families. The inventory reports 178 source declarations but selects 153 for this publication closure; this review does not claim 178 individual entry reviews.

The primary theorem has exactly the intended quantifiers and inequalities:

\[
\forall\,\lambda,v_0,v\in\mathbb R,\qquad
0<\lambda<1,\quad \lambda\pi<v_0<v,\quad
I_{\mathrm C}(v_0)\leq I_{\mathrm B}(v_0)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
I_{\mathrm C}(v)<I_{\mathrm B}(v).
\]

There is no added geometric-classification assumption, prior strict dominance, numerical margin, or assumed crossing. The result concerns the defined all-candidate profiles, not the unrestricted finite-perimeter isoperimetric profile. Existence of a crossing and the global minimizer classification are not conclusions of the Lean root.

## Evidence and proof correspondence

The two frozen Lean source files match every source-file SHA-256 in the inventory. All 153 declaration excerpts match their individual code hashes. A consistency check also verified a one-to-one correspondence among inventory entries, author classifications, and assembled supplement sections; each section contains the exact author statement and explanation and the exact frozen source excerpt. The assembled main body agrees with the handoff after replacing its reference tokens by the renderer's blocks, and all 110 reference-token occurrences resolve to inventory declarations. These checks establish provenance and coverage, not mathematical equivalence by themselves.

The statement/proof review establishes the analytic comparison independently of those mechanical checks. The finite type-(B) interval is \(0<\beta\leq\pi-\arccos\lambda\), while the type-(C) interval is \(0<b<\pi/2\). Their inverse charts recover every admissible angle. Type (B) retains the zero-radius endpoint and the obtuse-angle branch when \(R<\lambda\); type (C) is used only at positive radii. Positivity and monotonicity arguments preserve the distinction between nonnegative and positive radius domains.

The area-range proofs bracket every \(v>\lambda\pi\) between actual radius values, using \(R=0\) for the B lower endpoint and \(R=\lambda>0\) for the C lower endpoint. Strict area monotonicity and inverse-angle injectivity identify all competitors at that area. Thus the perimeter sets are nonempty singletons and their real infima equal actual candidate perimeters. The proof does not obtain the theorem from an empty infimum, a selected minimizing branch, or a totalized division at an excluded endpoint.

For the fixed-radius comparison, the exact perimeter gap is \(2H(\lambda,R)\). The direct positive-summand argument covers \(0<R\leq\lambda\). In the remaining region, density differentiation gives

\[
\partial_c\bigl(H(c,R)/c\bigr)=\frac{R}{c^2}L(c,R),
\qquad
\partial_cL(c,R)=-\frac{cN(c,R)}{\sqrt{1-c^2}D(c,R)^2}.
\]

The needed sign of \(L\) is restricted to \(0<c<\min(1,R)\). The proof includes the stationary locus \(N=0\): strict decrease of \(N\) makes it positive strictly to the left, so \(L\) has already decreased from \(L(0,R)=0\). When \(N<0\), the proof uses \(R>1\) and the negative left limit \(-b(R)\) at density one. For positivity of \(H\), the finite diagonal endpoint handles \(R<1\), while the zero ratio limit handles \(R\geq1\). The corner \(R=1\) has its own squeeze argument; the nonsingular \(R>1\) argument is not incorrectly reused there.

Both perimeter inverses have a strict common domain \(p>2\lambda\pi\), and their codomains carry positivity and the perimeter equation. Unique existence precedes choice. The same-radius comparison forces

\[
r_{\mathrm B}(p)<r_{\mathrm C}(p).
\]

The local gap theorem constructs a real representative at each \(p\), proves its local agreement on the genuine perimeter domain, and differentiates it using the inverse function theorem and \(A'=RP'\). It does not assert a single unrestricted global inverse. The derivative is

\[
G'(p)=r_{\mathrm B}(p)-r_{\mathrm C}(p)<0.
\]

Clamping is only a way to apply interval calculus to a real-valued representative. Its within-derivative at the clamping point is one-sided, exactly as the supplement says. Strict decrease of \(G\), strict increase of \(I_{\mathrm B}\), and the two proved profile-to-gap implications supply weak-to-strict persistence. The main proof follows this mechanism rather than assuming monotonicity of the equal-area perimeter difference.

## Model and geometric fidelity

CMV's type-(B) family encloses the unit disk; its two segment areas therefore receive the whole-disk correction \(-(1-\lambda)\pi\). The unit-circle boundary arc is weighted by \(\lambda\), consistently with the closed-disk density in the question. For type (C), the deficit is applied only to the overlap lens; its two segments have areas \(R^2S(b)\) and \(S(\pi/2-b)\). Direct comparison with the cited paper confirms the angular formulas and their radius reparametrizations.

The exact definition \(S(t)=t-\sin t\cos t\) is one unit-radius circular-segment area for central angle \(2t\). The source comment above `arcSegment` calls it twice that area, but the author correctly uses the actual definition, not that inaccurate comment. No factor-of-two defect propagates into the displayed formulas or derivative identities.

The formal files contain real analytic formulas, not measurable candidate sets or a formalized weighted-perimeter measure. The manuscript states this boundary of formalization. Its concluding implication for \(v_1=v_2\) is explicitly conditional on the external existence, regularity, connectedness, exhaustive candidate classification, and small-/large-area alternatives. Continuous strictly increasing area parametrizations yield continuous candidate profiles on the required range; combined with those external alternatives they give a meeting, and persistence rules out a later B return. This is a justified paper-level consequence under the stated external premises, not an additional unconditional Lean theorem.

## Certificate and declaration coverage

Every one of the 153 listed declarations has one review entry, with `source_sha256` set to that declaration's inventory `code_sha256`, and its informal statement copied exactly from the handoff. All declaration relations are equivalent after interpreting the author's explicitly declared notation. In particular, arbitrary-density algebraic/continuity statements remain distinguished from admissible-density sign statements; nonzero-radius analytic statements are not silently restricted to positive radius; and the local representative's existential and neighborhood quantifiers are preserved.

The configured generated-glob list, author family list, and inventory family assignments are all empty. No generated family representative or computational certificate ledger is missing. The frozen gate receipt reports a successful build and a primary-root axiom set consisting only of `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, and `propext`; the dependency audit reports exit code zero. Those are reported receipt facts, not a new compilation performed during this review and not substitutes for the semantic comparison above. No sampling or numerical plot is used as proof.

## External-source checks

The sole citation has a stable versioned locator: Cañete, Miranda Jr., and Vittone, *Some isoperimetric problems in planes with density*, arXiv:0906.1256v1, 8 June 2009. The online arXiv metadata confirms the title, authors, date, and version. The bundled PDF identifies that same version and date. Its printed pp. 32–33 contain Proposition 3.22 and the geometric classification; p. 34 contains Theorem 3.23, the following single-transition conjecture, and the B formulas; p. 35 contains Figure 19 and the C formulas; pp. 35–36 contain the small-/large-area comparison arguments. The locators used by the handoff are accurate. The external geometric results remain explicitly external premises; their complete geometric-measure-theory proofs are not certified by this analytic Lean closure.

## Findings and disposition

**Required publication correction — supplement only.** The author-supplied mathematical statements are repeatedly plain-text formulas rather than LaTeX. Concrete assembled examples are `LemmaSupplement.md:1647` (the perimeter-gap identity), `:1761` (the full B area formula), and `:2022` and `:2944`, which literally print `mathsf P_B(β)` and `mathsf P_C(b)`. The corresponding `informal_statement` fields contain these strings. The explanations make the mathematical meaning unambiguous, but their consequential evaluation identities are inline instead of the required displays. Typeset the mathematical expressions and place consequential identities in displays with their lead-ins. This is an author-content defect, not a renderer-owned wrapper defect and not a reason to change the formal mathematics.

No mathematical critical error, primary-theorem mismatch, main-proof critical error, or external-citation defect was found. The author main body starts with a second-level section, introduces the problem and citation before the exact theorem, keeps technical ledgers out of the narrative, and ends with the required scope limitation and bibliography. The supplement introduction is heading-free prose and explains the notation, empty generated-family coverage, total formulas, and domain restrictions. The assembled title, proof credit, repository locator, scaffolding, and reference blocks are expected renderer output and are not objections.

The analytic package is semantically equivalent to the frozen claim. Publication acceptance is withheld solely for the concrete supplement typesetting violation recorded above; it does not require changing hypotheses, root declarations, branches, or proof logic.
